summary: Anthropic released Claude Opus 5, a new version in its Opus model line, describing performance, pricing (unchanged from Opus 4.8), safety evaluation results, and new API features such as mid-conversation tool changes and automatic safety-classifier fallbacks.

practices.reason: The model shows stated, benchmarked gains on coding and knowledge-work tasks at lower cost per task than its predecessor, directly relevant to teams building coding and agentic products.
practices.quote: Opus 5 excels on valuable software engineering tasks. For example, on Frontier-Bench v0.1, Opus 5 surpasses all other models, and more than doubles Opus 4.8’s performance at a lower cost per task.

practices.reason: The lab discloses a purpose-built cyber capability evaluation (vulnerability discovery vs. exploitation) that a security team could use as a template for measuring model risk, though it is the lab's own instrument.
practices.quote: on OSS-Fuzz, an evaluation we’ve developed to assess how well models can find and then exploit vulnerabilities without extensive human guidance.

practices.reason: New API behaviors around tool changes mid-conversation and automatic safety-classifier fallbacks change how developers must design their integration and error-handling logic.
practices.quote: Mid-conversation tool changes on the Claude Platform. Within a conversation, developers can now change which tools Claude can use without invalidating the prompt cache.

notable_reason: This is a substantial new flagship-tier model release with extensive first-party benchmark, safety, and safeguard disclosures that AI industry watchers would want to see even absent an infrastructure signal.
